bullets.title: TSMC Q2 beats sharply; raises capex $100B, guides Q3 above consensus
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q2 EPS of $4.31 vs. $3.95 est ($3.98 adjusted vs. $3.89 est per internal tracking), revenue $40.2B vs. $39.3B est, and guided Q3 at ~$45.2B vs. $43B consensus. Chairman CC Wei confirmed FY2026 revenue to grow 'slightly above 40% YoY,' called AI demand 'extremely robust,' and announced an incremental $100B Arizona investment (2nm and below fabs + advanced packaging), bringing total US investment to $265B. TSMC also raised its dividend guidance 26-33% YoY through 2027.

bullets.title: TSMC A14 node on track; Agentic AI driving CPU demand renaissance
bullets.body: TSMC Chairman confirmed A14 (2nd gen nanosheet) offers 10-15% speed or 25-30% power improvement over N2 with ~20% density gain and is 'progressing well.' Separately, CC Wei noted that Agentic AI is driving a resurgence in CPU demand alongside AI accelerators, benefiting both x86 and Arm architectures — incremental silicon demand for TSMC.

bullets.title: UBS: TSMC capex hike reinforces AI supply chain confidence
bullets.body: UBS characterized TSMC's surprise capex increase as a strong positive signal for AI supply chain reliability, interpreting the move as TSMC's commitment to meeting surging AI infrastructure demand.

bullets.title: TSEM investing $3B in Japan for advanced packaging and silicon photonics by late 2027
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor announced up to $3B in Japanese capacity expansion, including $1B in Japanese government support, targeting 300mm silicon photonics, SiGe, and advanced packaging. First phase targets production readiness by late 2027. An analyst read suggests TSEM is 'building multiple wafer fabs for 2nm mass production' driven by strong multi-year U.S. customer demand.

bullets.title: NVIDIA CEO: 'We are still at the beginning of the cycle'
bullets.body: Jensen Huang reiterated at an event that the AI/GPU industry is still at the beginning of its cycle, implying significant demand runway ahead. Separately, Japan is building a national AI factory with NVIDIA featuring 13,750 Vera CPUs and 27,500 Rubin GPUs delivering 140 megawatts.

bullets.title: Goldman: AI agents could drive 24x token growth by 2030, worsening chip shortages
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs analysis suggests AI agents may produce a 24-fold increase in token consumption by 2030, with chip shortages expected to worsen over the next 12-18 months — a structural demand tailwind for GPU/chip suppliers.

bullets.title: Memory/storage stocks hammered; trader recommends calendar spreads
bullets.body: MU and SNDK are 'getting hammered again' pre-market with no material fundamental change in 72 hours. One trader recommended long-dated calendar spreads for AI infrastructure exposure, offering 'path-independent leverage without forced liquidation risk.'

bullets.title: South Korea rate hike triggers 6.4% Kospi drop; DRAM sector -25% from peak
bullets.body: Bank of Korea raised rates 25bps to 2.75% — its first hike in 3.5 years — triggering a 6.37% Kospi decline overnight. Hedgeye notes DRAM sector is now down 25.2% from cycle peak, with the crash view 'resumed.'

bullets.title: US lawmakers urge Trump to ban Chinese memory chips
bullets.body: US lawmakers are pressing the Trump administration to ban Chinese memory chips per the FT, a development that could reshape competitive dynamics in the DRAM/NAND market.

bullets.title: Iran threatens to close Bab el-Mandeb via Houthis if US strikes Iranian infrastructure
bullets.body: Iran has reportedly instructed Yemen's Houthis to prepare to shut the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — which carries 10-12% of global maritime trade — if the US strikes Iranian power infrastructure. This represents a second potential energy chokepoint alongside the Strait of Hormuz.

bullets.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3 model imminent: 2-3T parameters, open-weight, targets between Opus 4.8 and Fable 5
bullets.body: FT reports Chinese AI startup Moonshot will unveil K3 tonight — an open-weight model with 2-3 trillion parameters expected to outperform Anthropic's Opus 4.8 but fall short of Fable 5. This adds to substitution pressure on US AI capex leaders from cheaper Chinese models.

bullets.title: PPI internals show mixed signals: goods deflation, services sticky, PCE estimates lower
bullets.body: June PPI saw a 'massive decline' in goods m/m while services ticked higher. The portfolio management component came in 'surprisingly soft,' pulling down PCE price index estimates. However, processed intermediate material prices continue rising rapidly, suggesting downstream consumer goods inflation may accelerate.

bullets.title: Empire Manufacturing Index surges to 57.5 in July; capex outlook strengthens
bullets.body: Adjusted for ISM methodology, the Empire Manufacturing Index rose sharply to 57.5 in July, firmly in expansion territory. NY Fed survey respondents also reported a strengthened capex outlook, though it remains near historical midpoint.

bullets.title: BofA card data signals strong retail sales beat
bullets.body: Real-time BofA card spending data points to another beat in today's retail sales report, consistent with resilient consumer spending so far.

bullets.title: Record $2.8T notional OI set to expire in largest-ever monthly options expiration
bullets.body: With more than $2.8 trillion in notional open interest expiring, today marks the largest monthly options expiration on record — a potential source of heightened intraday volatility and positioning flows.

bullets.title: Tech rotation historical context: average rotation lasts 201 days; only 42 days in
bullets.body: One fintwit account notes the current tech sector rotation is only 42 days into what historically averages 201 days (based on 9 instances since 2000), implying ~4 months of potential headwind before capital flows back to tech.

bullets.title: Japan's largest foreign buyer of US stocks getting cold feet
bullets.body: Japan is reducing purchases of US equities amid valuation concerns and market volatility, potentially removing a key marginal buyer of US large-cap stocks.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex: sunk cost framing; depreciation to hit reported earnings, not cash
bullets.body: One analyst argues the 'can hyperscalers recoup AI investments?' question is irrelevant — the cash was already spent, and large depreciation charges will depress reported earnings without reflecting actual cash outflows. What matters is forward returns on incremental spending.

bullets.title: UBER launches $15B acquisition of Delivery Hero
bullets.body: Uber officially launched a $15B bid to acquire Delivery Hero, representing a major expansion of its food delivery footprint.

bullets.title: JPMorgan raises Corning price target to $200 from $185
bullets.body: JPMorgan lifted its Corning price target by $15 to $200, signaling continued bullish conviction likely tied to optical/fiber demand from AI data center buildout.
